title: deferred-fleet-supply-fence-and-rate-decoupler
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a supply-fence controller and rate decoupler to reduce noisy autoscaler churn and add high-cardinality utilization buckets for tenant throughput fidelity.
description:
Title: deferred-fleet-supply-fence-and-rate-decoupler

Description: Implement a supply-fence controller and an accompanying rate-decoupler layer for Dedicated fleet autoscaling. Motivation: during sustained but noisy demand patterns we observed oscillations in reserved capacity leading to repeated slot churn and increased tail latency for high-priority tenants. This PR introduces a short-lived supply fence that temporarily pins committed capacity while a statistical convergence window validates whether capacity adjustments should proceed, plus a rate-decoupler that separates admission rate signals from provisioning signals to avoid reactive overprovisioning. Key goals: reduce repeat provisioning cycles, improve p95/p99 latency stability for reserved tenants, and provide finer telemetry for utilization fidelity.

What changed (summary): added a supply-fence controller that opens/holds/closes fences per pool, implemented a deferred-fill adapter that queues provisional reservation intents and reconciles them only after the convergence window passes, added a rate-decoupler between admission controller and provisioner to smooth bursts, extended telemetry with per-tenant supply_fence events and high-cardinality utilization buckets, added operator docs and a rollout canary for Dedicated clusters. Includes unit, integration, and a targeted e2e canary test.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1729) - [x] Unit tests for fence lifecycle and reconciliation - [x] Integration tests against autoscaler simulator - [x] Telemetry plumbing and metric names approved - [x] Docs for ops + config knobs - [x] Canary deployed to 'dedicated-canary' and observed for 48h

Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c4: introduce supply-fence controller core loop and state machine - 2b3c4d5: deferred-fill adapter and convergence-window logic - 3c4d5e6: rate-decoupler shim and admission smoothing - 4d5e6f7: telemetry: supply_fence events, utilization bucketing and tagging - 5e6f7g8: docs: operators/dedicated_capacity.md and rollout notes - 6f7g8h9: tests: simulator scenarios for noisy-sustained and short-spike patterns

Files changed (high level): - pkg/autoscaler/supply_fence/controller.go (new): core fence lifecycle, backoff and TTL semantics - pkg/autoscaler/deferred_fill/adapter.go (new): accumulate provisional intents, convergence evaluation - pkg/autoscaler/rate_decoupler/shim.go (new): token-bucket based smoothing and token-credit ledger - telemetry/metrics/fleet_supply.proto (modified): new supply_fence_event, fence_state tags and tenant_id indexing - telemetry/collector/fleet_supply_collector.go (modified): emit fence open/close, hold reasons - docs/operators/dedicated_capacity.md (modified): operator knobs, safe defaults, rollbacks - tests/autoscaler/simulator/noisy_sustained_test.go (new): deterministic scenarios - deploy/overlays/dedicated-canary/kustomization.yaml (modified): canary config for convergence window

Behavioral notes and knobs: - default convergence_window: 30s (configurable per-pool) - fence_ttl: 300s to avoid long-term resource pinning; fences auto-expire if no progress - deferred_fill_threshold: only holds fills if provisional intent quota > 8% of pool capacity - rate_decoupler: separates 'admission tokens' (what tenants are allowed to submit) from 'provision tokens' (what can trigger scaling) with a default smoothing factor of 0.6 to bias toward stability over immediate provision - ops can set aggressive=false to favor latency over churn (not recommended for multi-tenant shared pools)

Telemetry and observability: - new metrics: redwood_fleet_supply_fence_total, redwood_fleet_supply_fence_duration_seconds, redwood_provisioner_decoupled_tokens, redwood_utilization_high_card_buckets - new labels/tags: pool_id, tenant_id (hashed), fence_state, hold_reason - dashboards: added a supply-fence panel (per-pool open/close rate) and a utilization fidelity histogram for tenant throughput distribution - alerts: temporary alert redwood.supply_fence.open_rate.high created to detect runaway fence churn during canary

Testing and canary: Canary ran in dedicated-canary for 48 hours with synthetic noisy sustained workload derived from SUP-3487. Observations: - provision churn down 62% compared to baseline - 95th percentile tenant latency improved by 12% during stabilization windows - no observable increase in overall overcommit risk (capacity headroom stayed within 3%)

Review conversation (excerpt, chronological): - Arjun Patel (reviewer): "Can the fence TTL be gated by pool priority? For critical pools we might want longer hold windows."
Author (Maya): "Good point — added pool-level override with sensible max of 15min; documented behavior and conservative default remains 5min/300s. See controller.go lines 148-172."
- Sofia Ramos: "The telemetry cardinality looks high because of tenant_id; did we hash tenant ids?"
Author: "Yes, tenant_id is hashed/hashed_salted_id before export; clarified in telemetry/collector comments and docs. We also bucketed high-card metrics to avoid cardinality explosion."
- Evan Liu: "Tests look good but add an integration scenario where the provisioner fails mid-convergence to ensure fences expire and reconciler recovers."
Author: "Added noisy_sustained_with_provisioner_fail test and fixed a small race on fence state transition."
- Arjun Patel: approved with comment: "Prefer monitoring thresholds be adjustable via feature flags; ops can tune quickly."
- Sofia Ramos: approved

CI summary: - unit (pkg/autoscaler/*): pass - integration (simulator): pass - static analysis/lint: pass after one fixed lint run - e2e canary smoke: pass - load-checks: pass with minor warnings (docker image build time flakiness retried automatically)

Migration and rollout plan: - stage 1: deploy supply-fence controller disabled by default (config=off) for 1 week to gather telemetry - stage 2: enable in dedicated-canary pools with conservative knobs (convergence_window=30s, fence_ttl=300s) for 48h - stage 3: enable default in low-risk pools for 72h; monitor supply_fence.open_rate and provisioner_decoupled_tokens - stage 4: gradual rollout to remaining dedicated pools with operator opt-outs documented - rollback: flip config to off and allow fences to expire; provider safe script included in docs/ops-rollback.sh

Backward compatibility and safety: - no API surface changes for public Redwood API. All controls are internal operator knobs. - added unit-tested feature-flag gating to avoid accidental global flips. - telemetry label hashing ensures no PII leaks.

Related issues and follow-ups: - Follow-up: ENG-1814 to add machine-learning based convergence window tuning - Follow-up: SUP-3521 to add alert-driven automated rollback if fence churn exceeds threshold

Merge: squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-26 after all approvals and green CI.

Notes for reviewers of record: This PR intentionally biases stability over immediate capacity responsiveness. Ops can tune defaults per-pool; please review the docs for suggested knob values before enabling in production pools.
